mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative investor sentiment and reduced S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent recessionary environments.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a strong supply-side economy, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts (HOUST) and falling retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which can lead to a short-term negative impact on S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings from retail.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of rising HOUST and falling RSAFS does not correlate with subsequent negative impacts on retail earnings.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent consumer confidence and spending boosts.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6%, it indicates a loose monetary policy in a weak labor market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to concerns about economic recovery.
regime_hint: loose monetary policy in weak labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent negative impacts on economic recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a strong demand-side economy, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or GDPC1 increase does not correlate with subsequent economic expansions.
